2027-01-06.title: 6 January · Wednesday after the Epiphany
readings: Every nation on earth will adore you, Lord
Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid
2027-01-06.alt: Christmas weekday. In countries where the Epiphany is not transferred to Sunday, today is the Solemnity of the Epiphany; the Eastern Churches celebrate the Baptism of the Lord (Denha). Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-06.verse: There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear; for fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not reached perfection in love.
theo: After feeding the five thousand, Jesus sends the disciples ahead by boat and goes up the mountain to pray. In the night the wind is against them and they strain at the oars. Early in the morning he comes to them walking on the sea. They think he is a ghost and cry out in terror. Then comes one of the most beautiful sentences in the Gospels: “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.” In Greek, “it is I” is egō eimi, the name God revealed to Moses. He climbs into the boat, and the wind ceases.

Mark adds an honest note: “they did not understand about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.” They had just seen a miracle and still did not see who Jesus was. St John gives the remedy for fear: “There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear.” God's love living in us, and our love for one another, is the only lasting answer to the storms of life. “No one has ever seen God; if we love one another, God lives in us.”
outline: Ask: what are you most afraid of this year?
Jesus on the mountain sees them straining.
God's love in us is the answer.
“Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
live: Tell Jesus in prayer the one fear that troubles you most this year.
Do one act of love today toward someone you are afraid of or avoid.
2027-01-06.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw your disciples straining at the oars and came to them across the sea. When the wind is against me, let me hear your voice: Take heart, it is I. Fill me with your perfect love that casts out fear. Amen.
altar: At Mass, after the Our Father, the priest prays that we may be “safe from all distress”. Christ steps into the boat of our lives in Holy Communion.

quick: Jesus prays on the mountain and sees us straining.
He comes across the storm: it is I, do not be afraid.
2027-01-06.action: Tell Jesus the one fear that troubles you most this year.
2027-01-06.question: Do I trust that Jesus sees me when I am straining at the oars?

family.explain: The disciples were in a boat in a strong wind at night. Jesus came walking on the water and said: do not be afraid, it is me! He got into the boat and the wind stopped.
family.intention: We pray for fishermen and all who travel by sea.
family.ask: Ask: “When do you feel afraid? Let us tell Jesus about it.”

illus: A fisherman from Vizhinjam was caught by a cyclone far from shore. For two nights he and his companions tied themselves to their boat. He said afterwards: I kept saying one line I learned as a child, Jesus, I trust in you. The wind did not stop at once, but the fear did.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you come to us in every storm and say: Take heart, it is I. Calm our hearts as we gather, and fill us with your love. Amen.
share: Jesus went up the mountain to pray (Mark 6:46). Do I believe that he prays for me?
Take heart, it is I (Mark 6:50). In what storm do I need to hear these words?
Perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18). How can love overcome a fear in my life?
interc: For the Church in times of persecution, that she may not be afraid.
For fishermen, sailors and all who travel.
For those who live in fear: of illness, of debt, of violence.
For our group, that our love may drive out fear.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son came to his disciples across the stormy sea. Come to us in our fears, and let your perfect love make us brave. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, after feeding the five thousand, Jesus sends his disciples ahead in the boat and goes up the mountain to pray (Mark 6:45–46). Even after a great success, he goes to the Father in prayer.

In the night the disciples are straining at the oars, for the wind is against them. Mark tells us that Jesus saw them (Mark 6:48). From the mountain, in the dark, he sees them. He sees you too, when life is hard work against the wind.

Early in the morning he comes walking on the sea. They think it is a ghost and cry out. Then he says: take heart, it is I; do not be afraid (Mark 6:50). The words it is I are the name of God revealed to Moses. The Lord of the sea climbs into their little boat, and the wind ceases.

Yet Mark says their hearts were hardened; they did not understand about the loaves. We too can see many signs of God's love and still be afraid. St John gives the remedy: there is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18).

Today, in many places, the Church celebrates the Epiphany, and our Eastern brothers and sisters celebrate the Baptism of the Lord. Christ is revealed as the one who comes to us in every storm. Let us invite him into our boat, and let his love drive out our fear. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus walked on the water to help his friends in the storm. When you are scared, say: Jesus, I trust in you! He is always near.

intro: Theme: “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
Christ comes across the storm; love casts out fear.

sub: He sees them in the dark.
q: He will not let your foot be moved; he who keeps you will not slumber. He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
After saying farewell to them, he went up on the mountain to pray.
points.apply: Pray each night this week for those who are struggling.

q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
for they all saw him and were terrified. But immediately he spoke to them and said, “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
points.apply: Repeat “Jesus, I trust in you” when fear rises.

sub: Hearts hardened in spite of signs.
God lives in us when we love.
q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear; for fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not reached perfection in love.
points.apply: Do one act of love toward someone you fear.

concl: The Lord of the sea climbs into our small boat.
Where love lives, fear loses its grip.
2027-01-06.resolve: Pray Psalm 27 each morning this week.
